$comment: Rebuilt 2026-08-16. The evidence behind every structural choice is in
HealthOS/knowledge/training-programme-evidence.md. If a decision here is not defensible from a
row in that file, it should not be here.
The four changes that matter:
1. EVERY MAIN PATTERN NOW APPEARS TWICE A WEEK, heavy on one day and light/technical on the
other. Pelland 2025 (67 studies, 2,058 participants): with volume equated, frequency has
negligible effect on SIZE but a 100% posterior probability of raising STRENGTH. Strength is
the stated non-negotiable ('I don't want to lose track of my main lifts'), so the main lifts
get the frequency and the arms and calves do not. Total sets per day are unchanged.
2. BB ROW AND OVERHEAD PRESS MOVED TO FRESH SLOTS. BB row sat 165 lb x 8 on 2026-05-25 and
165 lb x 8 on 2026-08-15: twelve weeks, zero movement, always the fourth or fifth block.
Overhead press went 60x10 to 65x7, which is net flat. Both now lead or sit second.
3. THE HANDSTAND LADDER IS GONE. Never logged once in 427 sets.
4. EVERY PAIRING IS NOW PHYSICALLY POSSIBLE, and a validator proves it rather than an author
remembering. See `station` on every exercise and equipment.json for the rule.
Frontal-plane work is loaded (lateral lunge, lateral bound, Copenhagen), not banded burnout.
Comert & Gruber 2025 found hip strengthening ALONE had minimal effect on knee alignment, which
is exactly what the banded lateral walk was. It is now insurance for the running, not a hobby.
Conditioning (run, bike, swim) is NOT in this file. It lives in conditioning.json because it is
not organised by gym day and does not share the set/rep/rest shape.
REBUILT 2026-08-21, after a per-session read of the watch export. Sessions run 81 to 120 minutes
with 45 to 75% of every one below 110 bpm, and Thursday 20 August contains a 28-minute hole
between squat set 3 and the next logged set. The sessions are long because of REST, not work:
roughly 4 to 5 minutes of actual lifting inside 81 minutes.
THE SUPERSETS WERE NOT SUPERSETS, and he said so himself. Eleven of the thirteen "alternate"
blocks were one real lift plus a band, a plank, a bridge or a carry, while the app told him
"Superset: alternate the two, rest once after both". They are now `pairing: "fill"`, which says
the true thing: do the partner IN the lift rest gaps, it adds no time. That is not a demotion,
it is the mechanism that shortens the session, and it is why these partners no longer consume a
time budget.
THE TWO "REAL PAIRS" THE ANALYSIS ASKED FOR ARE PHYSICALLY IMPOSSIBLE and were not built. It
called for chest press with row, and overhead press with pulldown. In this gym the row holds a
rack and the chest press holds a machine; the overhead press is at the dumbbells and the pulldown
at the cable stack. validate.mjs already refuses an alternate block that spans two zones or
occupies two fixtures, a gate written after the programme made that mistake five times. The
analysis was produced without the equipment model. Every existing pair is a lift plus a
fixture-free partner because that is the ONLY pair this gym physically permits, so the shape was
a constraint being obeyed rather than a defect. Two blocks are genuine loaded alternates and were
left alone: Monday split-squat with suitcase carry, and Monday lateral lunge with calf raise.
THE TYPED `time` FIELD IS GONE. It said "75-85 min" on days the app own budget model puts at 100
to 106, and the watch says his real sessions run 81 to 120. The typed string was the only one of
the three that nothing could check. It is computed and decomposed on the page now.
EVERY BLOCK CARRIES `why`, one line, required by the validator. He said the programme reads as
arbitrary because he had never seen the evidence file, and a programme he does not believe is one
he stops finishing. Where a block has no evidence behind it (calf raise, rotator cuff, Copenhagen
plank, biceps) the line says so rather than dressing it up.

monday.name: Monday
monday.title: Lower A: squat heavy, hinge light
monday.desc: Squat heavy, hinge light, sideways loaded

blocks.label: Power Primer

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.cue: Stand a forearm's length from the box. Swing the arms back, bend the knees about a quarter of the way, and jump ONTO the box. Land with both feet flat and knees bent, quietly. Then STEP down one foot at a time, never jump down. Success looks like: you hear almost nothing when you land, and you could hold the landing still for two seconds. If you land with a thud or stumble, the box is too high. Three reps only, because this is about speed, not tiredness.

alts.name: Lateral Bound
alts.cue: Hop sideways off one foot, land on the other, and freeze completely still for two seconds before hopping back. Only go as far as you can land and freeze. 3x4 each side.

alts.name: Pogo Hops
alts.cue: Small fast bounces off the balls of your feet. Keep the ankles stiff and the knees almost straight, like a skipping rope without the rope. 3x15.

alts.name: Explosive Step-Up
alts.cue: One foot on the box. Drive up fast enough that the other foot leaves the ground at the top, then lower slowly. No jumping, so no landing. Use this if anything hurts. 3x5 each leg.

blocks.why: Jumps first, while fresh. Deng 2024, 21 studies in untrained people: 0.61 for strength and 0.61 for aerobic fitness at 2 to 3 sessions a week. Box jump, not broad jump, because you step down instead of absorbing a landing.

blocks.label: Main Lift: Back Squat

exercises.name: BB Back Squat
exercises.cue: The lift we are progressing. Stance slightly wider than your hips with the toes turned out a little. Breathe IN and hold it, tighten your stomach like you are about to be poked, then sit down between your feet until the crease of your hip is below the top of your knee. Knees push out over your second toe, they do not fall inward. Stand up and breathe out at the top. Take a fresh breath and re-tighten before EVERY rep, not just the first.

alts.name: Smith Squat
alts.cue: The bar runs on rails so it cannot drift. Set your feet slightly in front of the bar. Same breathing, same depth.

alts.name: Front Squat
alts.cue: Bar rests on the front of your shoulders, elbows pointed forward and high. Because the weight is in front, your body stays more upright and depth comes easier. Much lighter than a back squat.

alts.name: Heavy Goblet Squat
alts.cue: Hold the heaviest dumbbell you can at your chest like a cup. The front weight balances you so you sit deeper. Use this if the racks are all taken.

alts.name: Leg Press
alts.cue: Feet shoulder width on the platform. Lower until your knees are near your chest without your lower back rounding off the pad, then press. Use this on a day your back is tired.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.cue: Done on the floor next to the rack while you rest between squat sets. Lie on your back, one heel pulled in close to your bum, toes pointed up, other leg straight out. Flatten your lower back into the floor, then push through the heel until your hips are level with your knee. Squeeze for two seconds at the top. LEFT leg first and give it one extra set. You should feel this in the back of your hip, not the back of your thigh: if it is all hamstring, bring the heel closer in.

alts.name: Frog Pump
alts.cue: On your back, soles of the feet together, knees fallen wide, heels close to you. Push the hips up and squeeze. 2x20.

alts.name: Banded Hip Abduction
alts.cue: Short band above the knees, seated on a bench or standing. Push the knees apart against the band and hold two seconds. 2x20.

blocks.why: Squat is one of the four patterns that earns twice a week. Pelland 2025, 67 studies: strength rises with frequency at matched volume (posterior 100%), size does not care about the split. The bridge goes in the squat rest, not on top of it.

blocks.label: Second Pattern: Hinge, light

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.cue: This is the SECOND time this week you hinge, and it is deliberately light: roughly what you did for 6 on Thursday minus 30 to 40 lb. The job is a clean groove, not a hard set. Bar touching your legs the whole way, knees slightly bent and then FROZEN. Push your hips backward toward the wall behind you until you feel a strong stretch down the back of your thighs, usually around knee height. Then squeeze your bum and drive the hips forward to stand. Stop the moment your lower back wants to round. No straps needed on this one: it is light on purpose, and if the bar is slipping at this weight the weight is wrong, not your hands.

alts.name: DB Romanian Deadlift
alts.cue: Two dumbbells in front of your thighs, same hip push backward. Good when the racks are busy.

alts.name: Back Extension
alts.cue: On the 45 degree pad. Hinge down and squeeze your bum to come up. Hug a plate for load.

alts.name: Kettlebell Swing
alts.cue: Same hip snap, done fast. Hike the bell back between your legs, then SNAP the hips forward so the bell floats to chest height. Arms do nothing. Start at 35 lb. 2x12.

blocks.why: The week second hinge, deliberately light. Frequency is what helps strength, so this is the cheap half of the hinge two sessions.

blocks.label: Single Leg + Anti-Lean

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides. Put the top of your back foot on the bench, laces down. Your front foot should be far enough forward that at the bottom your front shin is straight up and down, not leaning forward over your toes. Lower until your back knee is close to the floor. Drive up through the FRONT heel. The back leg is a kickstand, it does not push.

alts.name: DB Step-Up
alts.cue: Bench at about knee height. Drive up through the heel of the foot ON the bench. The trailing foot must not push off the floor. 8/leg.

alts.name: Reverse Lunge
alts.cue: Step straight backward, drop the back knee toward the floor, push through the FRONT heel to stand. Easier on the knees than stepping forward.

alts.name: Single-Leg Leg Press
alts.cue: One foot in the middle of the platform. Light enough that the working leg does all of it. 8/leg.

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry
exercises.cue: One heavy dumbbell in ONE hand, nothing in the other. Walk for the seconds shown standing as tall as you can. The whole exercise is refusing to lean toward the weight: imagine a broomstick down your spine that must stay vertical. Swap hands each set. This trains your side, which nothing else in the programme does. If you cannot stop leaning, the weight is too heavy.

alts.name: Farmer Carry
alts.cue: A heavy dumbbell in EACH hand, stand tall, walk. Easier to balance, trains grip harder, trains the side less.

alts.name: KB Suitcase Hold
alts.cue: One kettlebell in one hand, stand still and tall for the seconds shown. Use this if the floor is too crowded to walk.

blocks.why: Single-leg strength, and resisting sideways lean. Both loaded, both at the dumbbells, so these two genuinely alternate.

blocks.label: Sideways + Calves

exercises.name: DB Lateral Lunge
exercises.cue: This is the sideways movement you asked for, and it is loaded on purpose: unweighted band walks were shown to do little. Hold one dumbbell at your chest. Step wide to the LEFT and sit back into that left hip, keeping the right leg straight with the foot flat. Both feet stay pointing forward the whole time. Push off the left foot to come back. You should feel a stretch on the inside of the straight leg and work in the bent leg's hip. Start with a light dumbbell and a small step, then widen the step before you add weight.

alts.name: Cossack Squat
alts.cue: The deeper version. Same sideways sit, but let the straight leg's toes come up and go as low as you can. Bodyweight first, hold a dumbbell at the chest when it is easy. 3x6/side.

alts.name: Lateral Step-Up
alts.cue: Stand side-on to the box. Step UP sideways onto it with the near foot, drive through that heel, lower slowly. 3x8/leg.

alts.name: Banded Lateral Walk
alts.cue: Fallback only, on a day the dumbbells are all taken. Band above the knees, half squat, step sideways keeping the band tight. 3x10/side.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.cue: Done holding dumbbells on the floor by the bench, NOT on the calf machine, so this pairs with the lunge without occupying two machines. Stand on the edge of a step or a plate if you have one, heels hanging. Let the heels sink until you feel a stretch, pause one second at the bottom, then push all the way up onto your toes and squeeze for one second. Slow both directions. This is ankle insurance for the running.

alts.name: Machine Calf Raise
alts.cue: The standing calf machine, if nothing else in this block is running at the same time. Same full stretch and full squeeze.

alts.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
alts.cue: One leg at a time holding one dumbbell, full range. Harder, and closer to what running actually asks of the ankle. 3x12/leg.

blocks.why: Frontal-plane hip strength is injury insurance for the running: weak abductors feed pelvic drop, which feeds knee valgus, a documented route into shin and knee trouble in novice runners. The calf raise is not sourced.

tuesday.name: Tuesday
tuesday.title: Upper A: press heavy, pull moderate
tuesday.desc: Press heavy, pull moderate, shoulders looked after

blocks.label: Main Lift: DB Bench Press

exercises.name: DB Bench Press
exercises.cue: Feet flat on the floor. Pull your shoulder blades back and down into the bench and keep them there, like you are pinching a pencil between them. Breathe in, lower the dumbbells until you feel a good stretch across the chest, PAUSE for one second so there is no bounce, then press up and breathe out. The dumbbells travel slightly toward each other at the top but do not clang.

alts.name: BB Bench Press
alts.cue: Barbell version. Same shoulder blades, same pause on the chest. Easier to load heavy, harder on the shoulders.

alts.name: Machine Chest Press
alts.cue: Set the seat so the handles sit level with the middle of your chest. Same press, no balancing.

alts.name: DB Incline Press
alts.cue: Bench set one or two notches up from flat. Hits the top of the chest and the front of the shoulder more.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.cue: On the floor beside the bench, between press sets. Your example, and it is the pairing that always worked. On your back, arms straight up at the ceiling, knees bent up over your hips. Press your lower back FLAT into the floor and keep it there: that is the entire exercise. Slowly lower one arm behind your head and the opposite leg toward the floor, breathe out as they go. Stop the moment your lower back lifts off the floor, even if the leg is nowhere near down. Come back and swap sides.

alts.name: Hollow Body Hold
alts.cue: Lower back pressed flat into the floor, arms overhead and legs straight and lifted, so your body makes a shallow banana. Bend the knees or keep arms at your sides if the back lifts. 3x20s.

alts.name: Side Plank
alts.cue: On one forearm, body in a straight line from head to heels, hips lifted and held up. Drop to the knees if the hips sag. 3x30s per side.

blocks.why: Pressing twice a week, heavy here and moderate Friday. The dead bug goes in the rest gaps, and it is here for a reason rather than because core is good: core work moved knee valgus by d = -1.25 to -1.44, the same running insurance as the sideways work.

blocks.label: Second Pattern: Vertical Pull

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.cue: Sit tall with your thighs locked under the pad. Start with your arms fully straight so you feel the stretch down your sides. Pull your ELBOWS down toward your ribs rather than thinking about your hands, and bring the bar to your upper chest. Let it back up slowly and all the way straight. Building toward real pull-ups.

alts.name: Assisted Pull-up
alts.cue: Set enough counterweight that you get 8 clean reps with a full hang at the bottom and chin over the bar at the top. Reduce the assistance as it gets easy.

alts.name: Pull-up
alts.cue: The bar over the rack. Dead hang, chin over the bar, lower under control. As many clean reps as you have.

alts.name: TRX Row
alts.cue: Straps at the pull-up bar. Lean back with straight arms and a straight body, pull your chest to your hands. Walk your feet forward to make it harder, back to make it easier. 3x10.

blocks.why: The only vertical pull in the week, and the heavy pull is Friday. Nothing shares this rest window: the band that used to sit here is in the warmup now, where it is not a set anybody pretends to progress.

blocks.label: Seated Cable Row
blocks.why: The second horizontal pull of the week, and until 2026-08-22 there was no second one: BB Row on Friday was the only row in seven days, on a programme whose stated rule is that every main pattern happens twice (Pelland 2025, strength rises with frequency at matched volume). This is the slot the band pull-apart was occupying without loading anything.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.cue: Sit tall, knees soft, chest up. Start with your arms straight and let the weight pull your shoulder blades forward, then pull your ELBOWS back past your ribs and squeeze the shoulder blades together at the end. Do not lean back to move it: your torso stays where it started. Let it back out slowly until the arms are straight again.

alts.name: Chest-Supported DB Row
alts.cue: Chest on an incline bench so your torso cannot swing. Row both dumbbells to your ribs, elbows close, squeeze at the top.

blocks.label: Overhead

exercises.name: DB Overhead Press
exercises.cue: Moved earlier in the session because it has not moved in three months sitting at the back. Standing, dumbbells at shoulder height. Squeeze your bum and tighten your stomach BEFORE you press, so your ribs cannot flare and your back cannot arch backward. Press straight up until your arms are locked and the dumbbells are over the middle of your head, breathing out. If you have to lean back to finish, it is too heavy.

alts.name: BB Overhead Press
alts.cue: Barbell from the rack at collarbone height. Push your head slightly back so the bar clears your face, then forward under it at the top.

alts.name: Machine Shoulder Press
alts.cue: Seat height so the handles start level with your shoulders. Same lockout, no balancing.

alts.name: Seated DB Overhead Press
alts.cue: Bench upright, back supported. Takes the lower back out of it entirely.

exercises.name: Plank w/ Shoulder Taps
exercises.cue: On the floor beside the dumbbells. High plank on your hands, feet wide apart for balance. Slowly lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder, then put it back. The point is that your HIPS DO NOT ROTATE: if you filmed yourself from above, the belt line would stay square the whole time. Widen your feet if the hips twist. No weight on this one, it is bodyweight.

alts.name: Side Plank
alts.cue: On one forearm, body in a straight line from head to heels, hips lifted and held. Drop to the knees if the hips sag. 3x30s per side.

alts.name: Suitcase Carry
alts.cue: One heavy dumbbell in one hand, walk tall and refuse to lean toward it. Use this when the floor is busy. 3x30s per side.

blocks.why: Overhead pressing, the pattern with the least to show: 65x8 in July, back to 60x8 now. Plank in the rest gaps.

blocks.label: Triceps + Rotator Cuff

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown
exercises.cue: Cable high, rope or straight bar. Pin your elbows to your sides and keep them there: only the forearms move. Push down until the arms are completely straight, hold half a second, then let it come up slowly until you feel the stretch. If your elbows drift forward or you lean over the bar, drop the weight.

alts.name: EZ Bar Skullcrusher
alts.cue: Lying on a bench with the EZ bar. Keep the upper arms still and pointing at the ceiling, bend only at the elbow to lower the bar toward your forehead, then straighten. Light.

alts.name: Assisted Dip
alts.cue: Enough counterweight for 8 to 10 clean reps. Stay fairly upright to bias the triceps, lean forward to bias the chest.

blocks.why: Arms do not earn twice a week on the frequency evidence, so this is first to go when time is short. On a cable, so the number moves 5 lb at a time, which is the whole difference between this and the band that used to sit beside it.

thursday.name: Thursday
thursday.title: Lower B: hinge heavy, squat light
thursday.desc: Hinge heavy, squat light, sideways explosive

blocks.label: Power Primer

exercises.name: Lateral Bound
exercises.cue: Replaces the broad jump, which you swapped out every single time. This is the sideways explosive work you asked for. Stand on your LEFT leg. Push off it sideways and land on your RIGHT leg only, then FREEZE completely still for two seconds before going back. Land with the knee bent and pointing over your toes, never caving inward. Only jump as far as you can land and freeze. Success looks like: silent landing, no wobble, no second little hop to catch yourself. If you cannot freeze it, go shorter.

alts.name: Box Jump
alts.cue: Straight ahead instead of sideways. Jump onto the box, land soft and quiet with bent knees, STEP down. 3x3.

alts.name: Lateral Line Hop
alts.cue: The easier version. Both feet together, hop side to side over a line on the floor, small and fast, staying on the balls of your feet. 3x15.

alts.name: Pogo Hops
alts.cue: Small fast bounces on the balls of your feet, stiff ankles. 3x15.

blocks.why: Same reasoning and dose as Monday jumps, done sideways. First and fresh, progressed by quality and contact count rather than distance.

blocks.label: Main Lift: Romanian Deadlift

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.cue: The heavy hinge, the one we progress. Breathe IN and tighten your stomach. Bar stays touching your legs the whole way, shins vertical. Bend the knees slightly and then FREEZE them, then push your hips backward toward the wall behind you. Go down until you feel a strong stretch down the back of your thighs, usually around knee height, and no further. Squeeze your bum and snap the hips forward to stand up, breathing out at the top. If your lower back rounds you have gone too far down. STRAPS, because you asked on 18 August: yes, use them, and they will not cost you anything here. Do the first warm-up set with bare hands so you keep noticing what your grip is doing, then strap up for all four working sets. The hamstrings are what this lift is for, and stopping a set because the bar is slipping out of your fingers trains neither. Your grip is not being neglected either: the Farmer Carry on Friday and the Suitcase Carry on Monday are both held bare-handed and that is where grip is meant to be worked. This is standard coaching practice rather than something a trial has tested, so it is a convention, not evidence.

alts.name: DB Romanian Deadlift
alts.cue: Two heavy dumbbells in front of your thighs. Same hip push backward, same freeze in the knees.

alts.name: Smith RDL
alts.cue: Bar on rails so it cannot drift away from your legs. Useful for grooving the hinge when you are tired.

alts.name: Leg Curl
alts.cue: Direct hamstring work with no load on the lower back. Use it on a day your back is cooked. Squeeze at the top, lower slowly. 4x10.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.cue: On the floor by the rack between deadlift sets. Lie on your back, one heel close to your bum, toes up, other leg straight. Flatten your lower back into the floor, push through the heel until your hips are level with the knee, squeeze two seconds. LEFT first, one extra set. Should be felt in the back of the hip, not the back of the thigh.

alts.name: Frog Pump
alts.cue: Soles together, knees wide, heels close in. Push the hips up and squeeze. 2x20.

alts.name: Clamshell
alts.cue: On your side, band above the knees, knees bent. Open the top knee like a clam without letting your hips roll backward. 2x15/side, LEFT first.

blocks.why: The heavy hinge, the one that gets progressed. Squat went 135x10 to 185x6 since May on this heavy-then-light pattern. Bridge in the rest gaps.

blocks.label: Second Pattern: Squat, light

exercises.name: Front Squat
exercises.cue: Your second squat of the week, deliberately light. This is the technique fix: because the bar sits on the FRONT of your shoulders, your body is forced upright and depth gets easier, which is exactly what a back squat struggles with. Bar across the front of your shoulders, elbows driven forward and UP so the upper arms are near parallel to the floor. Let your fingertips just hook under the bar, the shoulders hold it, not the hands. Sit straight down, elbows stay high the whole time. If the elbows drop, the bar rolls forward: rack it and go lighter.

alts.name: Heavy Goblet Squat
alts.cue: Same upright effect with a dumbbell held at the chest, and no wrist or elbow demand at all. The easiest way to feel a deep upright squat.

alts.name: BB Back Squat
alts.cue: Light back squat instead, about 60% of Monday's weight. Use this if the front rack position hurts your wrists.

alts.name: Smith Squat
alts.cue: On rails. Feet slightly forward of the bar. Same depth, no balance demand.

blocks.why: The week second squat, light and technical. Same frequency argument as Monday light hinge.

blocks.label: Lunge + Core

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.cue: Dumbbells hanging at your sides, standing tall. Step straight BACKWARD, long enough that the back knee drops toward the floor and the front shin stays roughly vertical. Push through the FRONT heel to stand back up. Stepping backward rather than forward keeps the load off the front knee.

alts.name: Walking Lunge
alts.cue: Step forward into each lunge and keep travelling. Harder on balance and on the front knee. 8/leg.

alts.name: DB Step-Up
alts.cue: Bench at knee height, drive through the heel of the top foot. 8/leg.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.cue: On the floor next to where you are lunging. On your back, arms straight up, knees bent over the hips. Press your lower back FLAT into the floor and hold it there. Slowly lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg toward the floor, breathing out. The instant your lower back lifts, you have gone too far: come back and swap sides.

alts.name: Hollow Body Hold
alts.cue: Lower back pressed flat, arms overhead, legs lifted, body a shallow banana. Bend the knees if the back lifts. 3x20s.

alts.name: Side Plank
alts.cue: On one forearm, straight line head to heels, hips lifted. 3x30s per side.

blocks.why: Single-leg work, dead bugs in the rest gaps for the same knee-valgus reason as Tuesday.

blocks.label: Single-Leg Hinge + Groin

exercises.name: Single-Leg RDL
exercises.cue: Has sat at 40 lb since May, so this time the weight moves, not just the reps. One dumbbell in the hand OPPOSITE the standing leg. Stand on one leg with the knee slightly bent and frozen. Push the hip backward and let the free leg extend straight behind you like a see-saw, keeping your hips square to the floor: the back hip must not open toward the ceiling. Go until you feel the hamstring stretch, then stand and squeeze. Slow. Touch the bench with your free toe if you lose balance.

alts.name: B-Stance RDL
alts.cue: Back toe lightly touching the floor for balance, but almost all the weight on the front leg. Much easier to balance, so you can load it heavier.

alts.name: KB Single-Leg RDL
alts.cue: Same movement holding a kettlebell. The handle sits closer to your leg, which some people find easier to control. 8/leg.

exercises.name: Copenhagen Plank (short lever)
exercises.cue: The groin and inner-thigh half of the sideways work, and the piece nothing in the old programme trained at all. START WITH THE EASY VERSION: lie on your side with your bottom forearm on the floor, and put your TOP KNEE (not the foot) on the bench. Lift your hips off the floor so your body is a straight line, squeezing the bench with the top leg. Hold for the seconds shown. Your bottom leg hangs free. When 3 sets of 20 seconds feels controlled, move the top FOOT to the bench instead of the knee, which is much harder. Expect this to be humbling. Stop if you feel a sharp pull in the groin.

alts.name: Adductor Ball Squeeze
alts.cue: The gentlest version. On your back, knees bent, a ball or rolled towel between the knees. Squeeze it hard for the seconds shown and breathe. 3x20s.

alts.name: Side Plank w/ Leg Lift
alts.cue: Side plank on the forearm, then lift the TOP leg toward the ceiling and hold. Trains the outside of the hip instead of the inside. 3x20s per side.

blocks.why: Single-leg hinge, and the Copenhagen for the groin. The Copenhagen appears nowhere in the evidence file: common practice, not a trial.

friday.name: Friday
friday.title: Upper B: pull heavy, press moderate
friday.desc: Pull heavy, press moderate, swim catch

blocks.label: Main Lift: BB Row

exercises.name: BB Row
exercises.cue: This has been stuck at 165 lb since May because it always came fifth, when you were already cooked. It now leads the day, so it should move. Hinge forward until your chest is roughly parallel to the floor, knees slightly bent, back flat. Breathe in and brace. Pull the bar to your belly button by driving your ELBOWS backward past your ribs, then lower it all the way under control. Your torso does not move: if you are standing up a little to help the bar, it is too heavy.

alts.name: Chest-Supported Row
alts.cue: Chest on an incline bench, dumbbells hanging. The bench removes the lower back entirely, so nothing can cheat. Good on a day the RDLs left your back tired.

alts.name: Seated Cable Row
alts.cue: Tall chest, pull the handle to your stomach, squeeze the shoulder blades, let it stretch all the way forward.

alts.name: TRX Row
alts.cue: Straps at the pull-up bar. Body straight, pull your chest to your hands. Walk the feet forward to make it harder. 4x10.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.cue: On the floor at the rack, between row sets. This is the pairing that used to be lat pulldown plus dead bug, which was impossible: there is no floor at the cable stack. At the rack there is. On your back, arms up, knees over hips, lower back pressed flat into the floor. Lower one arm and the opposite leg slowly, stop before the back lifts, swap.

alts.name: Half-Kneeling Pallof Press
alts.cue: Band on the rack post at chest height. Kneel side-on, press the band straight out from your chest and refuse to be twisted. Hold two seconds. 3x10/side.

alts.name: Hollow Body Hold
alts.cue: Lower back flat, arms overhead, legs lifted, shallow banana shape. 3x20s.

blocks.why: Pulling twice a week, heavy here and moderate Tuesday. Six loaded pulling sets in a week is the thinnest part of the programme, which is why this is the spine of the day and not the chest press.

blocks.label: Second Pattern: Horizontal Press

exercises.name: Machine Chest Press
exercises.cue: Your second press of the week, moderate rather than heavy: Tuesday is the day the bench gets pushed. Machine on purpose, so a tired chest does not have to balance dumbbells. Set the seat so the handles line up with the MIDDLE of your chest. Press out until the arms are straight without locking hard, then come back slowly until you feel the stretch. Shoulder blades stay pinned back against the pad.

alts.name: DB Incline Press
alts.cue: Bench one or two notches up from flat, dumbbells. More work for the top of the chest and the shoulders.

alts.name: Chest Fly Machine
alts.cue: Elbows slightly bent and fixed, bring the arms together in front of you and squeeze for one second. Stretch, not a press.

alts.name: Assisted Dip
alts.cue: Lean your chest forward to bias the chest. Enough counterweight for 8 clean reps. You had 5 strict dips in May, so this is trackable.

blocks.why: The second press of the week, moderate. It CANNOT share a window with the row: the row holds a rack and this holds a machine, and the validator refuses the pairing.

blocks.label: Assisted Pull-Up
blocks.why: The second vertical pull. Lat Pulldown on Tuesday was the only one in the week, against the same twice-a-week rule the rest of the programme follows. The counterweight is the load and it goes DOWN as you get stronger, which is a progression with a finish line: an unassisted pull-up.

exercises.name: Assisted Pull-Up
exercises.cue: Set the counterweight so you get 6 clean reps: full hang with straight arms at the bottom, chin over the bar at the top. Log the COUNTERWEIGHT, and remember it is the one number here that should go DOWN over time. When 6 feels easy, take 10 lb of assistance off.

alts.name: Lat Pulldown
alts.cue: If the assisted machine is taken. Same job, elbows down to the ribs, all the way straight at the top.

blocks.label: Machine Shoulder Press
blocks.why: The second overhead press. DB Overhead Press on Tuesday was the only one, and it is the pattern with the least to show for the year: 65x8 in July, back to 60x8 now. A machine on the second exposure keeps it cheap and lets the dumbbells stay the day that gets pushed.

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.cue: Set the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height, not above your ears. Press up until your arms are straight without shrugging, and come back down slowly until the handles are level with your shoulders again. Stop the set when your lower back starts arching off the pad.

alts.name: Seated DB Overhead Press
alts.cue: Bench upright, dumbbells at shoulder height, press up and slightly together. Ribs down, no arch.

blocks.label: Swim Catch + Rotator Cuff

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
exercises.cue: This is your freestyle catch trained directly, which is why it stays even though the rest of the day changed. Cable set high, rope or straight bar, stand back a step and hinge slightly forward. Arms stay STRAIGHT the whole time, elbows barely bent and locked there. Sweep the bar down in an arc to your thighs and squeeze the muscles down the sides of your back, then let it float back up. Much lighter than a lat pulldown, because straight arms are a long lever.

alts.name: Band Straight-Arm Pulldown
alts.cue: Band anchored high on a rack post. Identical arc with straight arms. Use it when the cables are all busy.

alts.name: DB Pullover
alts.cue: Lying across or along a bench, one dumbbell held over the chest with near-straight arms. Lower it behind your head until you feel the stretch under the armpits, then pull it back over. 3x12.

blocks.why: Straight-arm pulldown for the catch position in the water. Not sourced in the evidence file, and it stays because it is loadable and it is the one lift here aimed at the swim.

blocks.label: Biceps, then Carry

exercises.name: EZ Bar Preacher Curl
exercises.cue: The zed bar with the seat, which you have had all along and which was never written down anywhere. Sit with the backs of your upper arms flat on the slanted pad and keep them there. Grip the angled part of the bar so your wrists sit comfortably. Curl up until your forearms are vertical, squeeze, then lower ALL THE WAY until the arms are straight. The pad is the point: it makes swinging impossible, so the weight will feel heavier than a standing curl. Start lighter than you think.

alts.name: DB Bicep Curl
alts.cue: Standing, dumbbells, elbows still at your sides, no swinging. Squeeze at the top, lower slowly.

alts.name: Cable Curl
alts.cue: Low cable with a straight or EZ attachment. The cable keeps tension on the muscle at every point, including the top where dumbbells go light. 3x12.

alts.name: Hammer Curl
alts.cue: Thumbs up the whole way, like holding two hammers. Hits the forearm and the outside of the arm too.

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
exercises.cue: Done after the curls rather than alternating with them, because it needs room to walk and the preacher seat does not travel. A heavy dumbbell in each hand, stand as tall as you can, shoulders back, stomach tight, and walk for the seconds shown. Grip, posture and everything down your sides at once. Put them down before your form falls apart, not after.

alts.name: Suitcase Carry
alts.cue: One dumbbell only. Much harder on the side you are NOT carrying, because it has to stop you leaning. Swap hands each set.

alts.name: KB Farmer Carry
alts.cue: Kettlebells instead, up to 50 lb each. They hang differently and swing a little, so the grip works harder.

alts.name: DB Static Hold
alts.cue: Heavy dumbbells held at your sides, standing still and tall for the seconds shown. Use this when the floor is too crowded to walk.

blocks.why: Arms do not need twice a week. The farmer carry is the week grip work, held bare-handed, which is why straps on Thursday heavy RDL cost you nothing.
